result:
I lofted the 50 slices into one solid and exported it to `/lab/out/terrain.stl`. I didn't re-open the STL to check it.

**Orientation fix:** the sketches have their local Y axis pointing along −Z, so the first loft hung below the XY plane (z from −33.17 to 0). I mirrored it across XY, which puts it right way up. North was already at +Y, since slice 1 sits at y = 114.81 and slice 50 at y ≈ 0. The mirror left the original body in place, so I deleted that. The STL contains only the flipped body.

**Volume:** 166,209 mm³ (surface area 27,977 mm²).

**Bounding box:**
- X: 0 to 100
- Y: 0 to 114.81
- Z: 0 to 33.165

The base is flat at z = 0.

**Highest point:** (x, y, z) ≈ **(44.19, 44.52, 33.165)**. This is a slice vertex, at x = 44.186 on slice 31 (y = 44.5176), where z is 33.1646. The smoothed loft peaks about 0.0007 mm higher, at 33.1653.

The loft has 48 faces: five planar and 43 curved.

The bounding-box maximum, 33.1653, sits slightly above any real surface point, so a slab test at z ≥ 33.1 found nothing. I used a slab at z ≥ 31 to bracket the peak, then read the exact vertex from slice 31. Both slab tests were undone, so the design contains only the mirrored terrain body.
